Since the incomplete automobile manufacturer has control over the production of only part of the automobile, it must specify guidelines as to the manner of the automobile's completion in order to ensure that the fuel economy level it has assigned to the automobile remains accurate. Information that must appear on the fuel economy labels required under Section 506 will, to the extent possible, be compiled and attached to the automobile by the incomplete automobile manufacturer. In the event that the final stage manufacturer completes the automobile so that the test weight is exceeded, that manufacturer would then become the manufacturer of the automobile for the purposes of Title V.
Section 502(b) of Title V requires the Administrator to issue AFES's for nonpassenger automobiles manufactured in model years which begin more than 30 months after the date of enactment (December 22, 1975) of Title V. My 1979 is the first MY that begins after the 30-month period. As a minimum, Title V requires that an AFES for nonpassenger automobiles of not more than 6,000 pounds GVWR must be issued for that MY. Section 502(b) provides that the AFES must be issued 18 months before the beginning of MY 1979.
